clue.text: Just ghastly! Behead it!

indicators.note: an order to cut off the head means the first letter of the word for ghastly goes

parts.note: something ghastly is frightful

explanation.surface: An outraged cry demanding an execution be carried out on something awful.
explanation.definitionFit: Rightful and just both describe a claim that is fair and proper.

clue.text: Ushers disrupted first film show

indicators.note: disrupted letters are thrown out of order

explanation.surface: Cinema attendants upset the opening screening.
explanation.definitionFit: Rushes are the first prints of a day's filming, viewed before editing.

clue.text: Swelling with blood all round it

indicators.note: the word for blood surrounds the other word

parts.note: gore is spilt blood

explanation.surface: A swollen wound covered in blood.
explanation.definitionFit: A goitre is an enlargement of the thyroid gland showing as a swollen neck.

clue.text: Large attic in disorder

indicators.note: in disorder the letters lie jumbled and need rearranging

explanation.surface: A big loft in a mess.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' joins the fodder: rearrange ATTIC IN.
explanation.definitionFit: Titanic means gigantic, like the Titans of myth.

clue.text: Forearmed with this?

parts.note: a play on forearmed: one bone of the lower arm gives the forearm its arming

explanation.definitionFit: The ulna is one of the two bones of the human forearm.

clue.text: Banker takes drink back to student quarters

parts.note: a river has banks, so a banker is a river, here the Cam of Cambridge

indicators.note: going back means the word for drink is turned round

parts.note: to sup is to drink

explanation.surface: A bank employee brings a drink back to halls of residence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns SUP into PUS. The Cam is the river through Cambridge, a crossword favourite for 'banker'.
explanation.definitionFit: A campus is the grounds of a university where its students live and study.

clue.text: Retorts holding solutions

explanation.definitionFit: Answers are both replies to a remark and solutions to questions.

clue.text: Frustrated pal takes rouser, yet remains unaroused

indicators.note: frustrated letters are thwarted and jumbled

parts.note: a tonic rouses and invigorates

explanation.surface: A thwarted friend tries a stimulant but stays unexcited.
explanation.definitionFit: A platonic relationship stays affectionate but without sexual desire.

clue.text: Encounter Sikhs involved in border disturbance

indicators.note: the Sikhs' letters get tangled up with the border word
disturbance stirs the combined letters into a new order

parts.note: a rim is an edge or border

explanation.surface: Sikh troops meet trouble during a frontier disturbance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'involved in' mixes the word for border into SIKHS, and 'disturbance' shuffles the pool SIKHS plus RIM.
explanation.definitionFit: A skirmish is a brief fight, a minor clash between forces.

clue.text: Running through — it's an unhygienic action

definitions.meaning: piercing meat on a spit, skewering it

explanation.definitionFit: Spitting means both impaling on a spit and expelling saliva, a dirty habit.

clue.text: Black soldier-king in an oriental garment

indicators.note: one piece sits inside the garment word

parts.note: a sari is the wrapped garment worn in South Asia
K is the chess abbreviation for king

explanation.surface: An African ruler who was once a soldier is dressed in Eastern robes.
explanation.definitionFit: An askari was an African soldier serving under colonial European command in East Africa.

clue.text: Composer of "Three Little Girls'

parts.note: three short girls' names: Vi, Val and Di
three short girls' names: Vi, Val and Di
three short girls' names: Vi, Val and Di

explanation.surface: Who wrote a song called Three Little Girls?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Little' means shortened names: Vi (Violet), Val (Valerie) and Di (Diana).
explanation.definitionFit: Antonio Vivaldi was the Venetian Baroque composer of The Four Seasons.

clue.text: Royalty make a noisy fuss when travelling

parts.note: ER, Elizabeth Regina, stands for the Queen and so royalty
to rant is to shout and complain loudly

explanation.surface: A royal personage kicks up a fuss on tour.
explanation.definitionFit: Errant in its old sense means wandering, as a knight errant roams in search of adventure.

clue.text: Pest a menace to cables?

definitions.meaning: a beetle larva that damages crop roots
jokily, a worm that would eat through wires

explanation.definitionFit: The wireworm is a click-beetle larva harmful to crops; read literally it is a worm attacking wires.

clue.text: Top person getting on in a demonstration

indicators.note: one word set inside the protest word

parts.note: a march is a protest demonstration

explanation.surface: A leading figure joining a protest march.
explanation.definitionFit: A monarch is the sovereign, the person at the very top of a state.

clue.text: Students with fruits of their endeavour

definitions.text: Students with fruits of their endeavour

parts.note: scholars are people who study
hips are the fruits of the rose

explanation.surface: Learners rewarded for their hard work.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines the answer: grants won by students as a result of their efforts.
explanation.definitionFit: Scholarships are awards earned by able pupils, a reward for their academic effort.

clue.text: Hero suffers anguish — sick at heart

indicators.note: at heart puts the illness word in the middle of the other piece

parts.note: to ache is to suffer pain
ill means sick

explanation.surface: A hero in torment, sick to the core.
explanation.definitionFit: Achilles was the great Greek hero of the Trojan War.

clue.text: Puzzling anagram for cold drink

indicators.note: puzzling letters are confusingly rearranged

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for cold on taps

explanation.surface: A tricky wordplay device in exchange for a cool drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Armagnac is a brandy distilled in Gascony, France.

clue.text: Chiropodist, maybe, holding his head — now dealing with ears

indicators.note: the description of the foot doctor wraps round one letter

parts.note: a chiropodist treats corns, so could be called a handler of corns
his refers to the chiropodist, whose first letter is C

explanation.surface: A foot specialist cradles a patient's head while working on ears.
explanation.walkthrough: 'his head' is the head of the chiropodist, C; 'maybe' marks a whimsical description. A corn chandler is a dealer in grain, the ears of corn.
explanation.definitionFit: A corn chandler is a merchant selling grain, which grows in ears.

clue.text: Order to view?

parts.note: the invitation come and see run together

explanation.definitionFit: A command is an order, and the word sounds like the first part of the imperative to come and look.

clue.text: See vagrant in dock obscure the issue

indicators.note: the docking word sits inside the other letters
a vagrant wanders, so the letters stray into another order

parts.note: to dock a tail is to clip it

explanation.surface: Spot a tramp in the dock clouding the matter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'vagrant' mixes SEE into E..SE, with CLIP set in.
explanation.definitionFit: To eclipse is to overshadow or block out, hiding something from view.

clue.text: Stone upturned — small creatures beneath

indicators.note: the creatures come below the first piece in a down answer

parts.note: up turned over reads backwards
mice are small rodents

explanation.surface: A stone is turned over to find little animals underneath.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upturned' is up turned over, giving PU.
explanation.definitionFit: Pumice is a light porous volcanic stone.

clue.text: Tends to edge to the sun

parts.note: a verge is an edge
S is short for sun, as in Sunday

explanation.surface: Gardener tends the lawn edge facing the sun.
explanation.definitionFit: Verges, as in verges on, means leans towards, as tends does.

clue.text: Seeing that a chum's in trouble

indicators.note: being in trouble suggests things stirred up, so the letters before it are mixed

explanation.surface: Because a friend is in difficulties.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is part of the fodder, not a link: rearrange A CHUMS IN.
explanation.definitionFit: Inasmuch as means since or because, a formal way of saying given that.

clue.text: With bud opening, parasite may slip over the trunk

indicators.note: the opening of a word is its first letter

parts.note: a louse is a parasitic insect

explanation.surface: A bug on a budding plant may glide over the tree's trunk.
explanation.walkthrough: The trunk is the human torso, not a tree's.
explanation.definitionFit: A blouse is a woman's top, a garment pulled over the upper body.

clue.text: Noble has right to entertain the monarch

indicators.note: entertaining a guest means holding them inside

parts.note: what is due is what one has a right to
K stands for king

explanation.surface: A nobleman has the right to host the king.
explanation.definitionFit: A duke is the highest rank of the British peerage.

clue.text: Conveyance of property to the French

parts.note: land is real estate, landed property
au is French for to the

explanation.surface: Legal transfer of real estate to French buyers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Conveyance' in a legal surface suggests a property transfer, but here it is a vehicle.
explanation.definitionFit: A landau is a four-wheeled horse-drawn carriage, a means of transport.

clue.text: Dispose of fish and doughy food

parts.note: to dump is to get rid of
ling is a fish of the cod family

explanation.surface: Throw away the fish and the stodgy food.
explanation.definitionFit: A dumpling is a small ball of boiled or steamed dough.

clue.text: Notice takes about a month — then you withdraw

indicators.note: the word for notice takes in another piece

parts.note: to notice is to see

indicators.note: about means the month abbreviation is turned round

parts.note: Dec is short for December

explanation.surface: A notice period of about a month must pass before you leave.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' is the reversal signal here, though it could pass for the circa abbreviation C; 'takes' is the container signal, and 'then you' only links the wordplay to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To secede is to formally withdraw from a federation or organisation.

clue.text: Free-ranging prophet rejected judgements made by them

indicators.note: free-ranging letters roam about and settle in a new order
rejected here means the prophet is turned back to front

parts.note: a seer foresees the future

explanation.surface: A wandering prophet turned down the verdicts given.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ranging' mixes FREE into REFE; 'rejected' turns SEER into REES.
explanation.definitionFit: Referees are the officials who adjudicate, so judgements come from them.
